transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm seeking help because I've been feeling extremely depressed and down for the past few months. On top of that, I've been hearing and seeing things that other people don't for nearly two years now.
Can you tell me more about when your depressive feelings started and how they relate to when you began hearing and seeing things that others don't?

My struggles have been going on for about 1 year and 10 months in total. My current depressive episode started about 3 months ago, but the voices and visions have been happening on and off for nearly two years. Even when I'm not feeling depressed, I still hear and see things.

For the periods when you're not feeling depressed, do the voices and visions interfere with your daily life, work, or social relationships, or are you able to manage them and function relatively normally?

Yes, even when I'm not feeling depressed, the voices and visions are incredibly distracting and terrifying. They make it almost impossible to focus on my work or have normal conversations with people, so I really struggle to function. It feels like I can never escape them, no matter how my mood is.
Can you estimate how much of the past two years you've spent experiencing depressive symptoms versus periods where you didn't have significant depression, but still had the voices and visions?

I would say I have felt deeply depressed for the vast majority of the past year and ten months. There was only a brief period of about two or three weeks where my mood felt relatively normal or okay, but I was still hearing voices and seeing things during that time.

Did the depressive symptoms seem to dominate the clinical picture for most of the time you've been experiencing both depression and psychotic symptoms, or were there extended periods where the psychotic symptoms were prominent without significant depressive symptoms?

Yes, the depression has definitely dominated the picture for the vast majority of the past year and ten months. The only exception was that brief period of about two to three weeks where I didn't feel depressed at all, but I was still hearing voices and feeling watched. Other than those few weeks, the heavy depression has been there almost constantly alongside the other issues.
Do you think the voices and visions would improve or lessen if your depressive symptoms were effectively treated, or do you feel they are separate issues that would persist regardless of your mood?

I feel like they are somewhat separate issues. Even during that brief time when my depression lifted, the voices and visions still persisted on their own. It seems like they don't completely depend on my mood and would probably still be there.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you didn't experience any depressive symptoms, and if so, did the voices and visions continue during that time, or did they also improve or disappear?

Yes, there was a period of about two or three weeks where my mood felt normal and I didn't feel depressed at all. However, the voices and visions definitely continued during that time and didn't improve or go away. They remained just as intense even when my mood was okay.

Can you confirm that for a substantial portion of the time, more than half of the total duration of your illness, you have had significant psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations, in the absence of a major depressive episode?

Actually, it is the other way around. I have had the depressive symptoms for the vast majority—more than half—of the total duration of my illness. It was only during that brief two to three week period that I experienced the hallucinations and delusions without any depression.
Is there anything else you'd like to share or any other symptoms you're experiencing that we haven't discussed, which might help in understanding your condition better?

Lately, I've also been feeling completely empty and emotionally numb, like I can't feel any warmth or sadness at all. On top of that, I constantly worry that people are monitoring or watching me, which makes me want to isolate myself from everyone. I also find myself having passive thoughts of wishing I wouldn't wake up in the morning.
Can you describe in more detail what you mean by feeling like people are monitoring or watching you, and how this symptom relates to your depressive feelings and the voices or visions you experience?

I constantly feel like I am being watched and monitored by others, which makes me feel extremely unsafe and feeds into my deep depression. I also hear voices and see things that aren't there, and these terrifying experiences make my depression much worse. However, even when I am not feeling deeply depressed or sad, the voices and the feeling of being watched still persist on their own for weeks.
